title: Question to my workflow
author: Finn_Karak
selftext:
I’m still pretty new to AI-assisted game dev, so I’m curious how other people are doing this.  
My current workflow is pretty simple:

I use ChatGPT to plan features, think through systems, and write more precise prompts for OpenCode.

The idea is to give OpenCode enough context so it doesn’t waste a bunch of usage just rereading the whole project.

OpenCode does the actual coding and gives me a report with the changes and test results.

I bring that back to ChatGPT, go over it, and make a smaller follow-up prompt if something needs fixing.

So basically, ChatGPT is my planner/reviewer and OpenCode is the one actually working on the code.

I’m still pretty new to all of this, so I’d love to hear how you guys handle your AI game dev workflow.

Any tips or tricks to make this more efficient?  
And what AI models or coding tools would you recommend right now, especially if limits and cost matter?

comments.author: BoltVnderhuge
comments.body: One thing I’d add are saving documents outlining themes/mechanisms/features and how they are implemented that can always be referenced by the models as you revisit things.

replies.author: Finn_Karak
replies.body: Thats actually really helpfull and i havent thought about that. Tysm <3

comments.author: forgetscode
comments.body:
I've never heard of OpenCode but why not just use one harness? If you want to use multiple models just have your main model use a CLI for the other. Anything some third party service gives you, just set it up yourself in house for more flexibility, even memory management, ask your frontier model to design your workspace for how you want to work, then you also gain the advantage of knowing exactly what's going on when your agents work instead of being confused why something happened.

I personally use claude code for majority of work but for game dev Chat GPT is a must imo.

Cost wise definitely go with Grok as you can do everything with it and its cheaper.

replies.author: Finn_Karak
replies.body:
Tysm in advance for your time.

I've never worked on a game before, especially not with AI, so I also have no idea what a CLI is. The way I ended up using both together just developed naturally over time, and since it worked, I simply kept working that way.

I would also be willing to pay for Claude or another model, but there are so many different models being recommended everywhere that I'm honestly unsure which one I should actually use. I also don't want to waste money unnecessarily.

If you want, you're also very welcome to take a look at my project. I uploaded it earlier.

replies.author: forgetscode
replies.body:
CLI - Command line interface. Basically controls your computer and that means a claude interface or other could use a codex interface on its own.

Claude cannot generate art. I use both GPT and Claude together and I think most people would consider my setup expensive.

Grok can code and generate art at good quality and it's cheaper plans are very generous so I would recommend that setup if costs matter to you.

comments.author: CashewSwagger
comments.body:
Never used open code. Im rocking the 20$ plan for Claude and codex. So here's my setup 

Claude:
Opus 4.6 plans. Haiku reads code base and provides context. Sonnet writes code. 

Codex: Astra checks this new code against all existing systems and adjusts as needed. 

If I need assets I draw them myself or Astra is very capable of making some.
